rules.rationale: Lower B-type natriuretic peptide levels are associated with mild CAP (PSI class I, II, or III).

rules.rationale: Procalcitonin levels increase with increasing severity of CAP, classified according to the PSI score.
Procalcitonin levels on admission are significantly higher in patients who die during follow-up compared to survivors.
Procalcitonin has a higher AUC for predicting survival compared to PCT, CRP, and total leukocyte count.
A clinical model including the PSI and procalcitonin increased prognostic accuracy to predict failure compared with a model relying on the PSI alone.
